name: Hans Gerling

summary.text: Hans Gerling was the head of the Cologne insurance group Gerling-Konzern and, with Herbert Quandt and Emil Georg Bührle, a financier of Iwan David Herstatt's Bankhaus Herstatt, in which Gerling held the majority of the shares. After the bank was closed by German regulators on 26 June 1974 with foreign-exchange losses far exceeding its capital, Gerling was forced to sell his majority stake in the insurance group and give up his post as chief executive.

facts.claim: Hans Gerling, together with Herbert Quandt and Emil Georg Bührle, financed Iwan David Herstatt's bank and held a majority share in it.
German regulators forced Bankhaus Herstatt into liquidation on 26 June 1974 after speculative foreign-exchange positions produced losses of about DM 470 million against capital of DM 44 million.

sources.title: BIS Quarterly Review, December 2002: Herstatt and settlement risk
Financial Stability Review, December 2007, Box: Herstatt

facts.claim: After the collapse Gerling was forced to sell his majority stake in the insurance company and relinquish his post as chief executive.
facts.quote: he was forced to sell his majority stake in the insurance company and relinquish his post as chief executive

facts.claim: The Hans-Böckler-Stiftung's account states that the bank's foreign-exchange department worked largely without control, trader limits were circumvented and losses were hidden from the accounting department.
facts.quote: Die Devisenabteilung arbeitete weitgehend ohne Kontrolle, Händlerlimits wurden umgangen, Verluste vor der Buchhaltung verheimlicht.

connections.claim: Gerling financed Herstatt's bank and was its majority shareholder.
Dattel headed the foreign-exchange department of the bank in which Gerling held the majority.

openQuestions: Site claim tested: 'majority shareholder' is supported; 'supervisory-board chairman' was not confirmed by sources found.
